hook.text: Alexander Fleming warned in 1945: misuse antibiotics and bacteria will evolve resistance. He was exactly right.

buildup.text: Antibiotics kill susceptible bacteria. Resistant mutants survive and multiply. Within weeks, resistance can dominate.

discovery.text: MRSA evolved resistance to methicillin in just two years after the drug launched. Evolution outpaced medicine.

twist.text: Bacteria share resistance genes through horizontal transfer—no sex needed. One resistant cell can arm its neighbors.

climax.text: The WHO calls antibiotic resistance a top global health threat. By 2050, it may kill 10 million people yearly.

punchline.text: We gave bacteria a challenge. They evolved the answer.

quiz.question: How do bacteria share resistance genes?
